title: Stride-aligned prefetch & comm-window manager for asymmetric stage pipelines
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background:
Multi-GPU prefill/decode pipelines exhibit high tail latency when stage handoffs and collective comms (NCCL) are poorly aligned with per-stage kernel pacing. Current approaches either over-serialize handoffs (increasing latency) or generate microbursts that saturate interconnects. We need a scheduler that minimizes end-to-end prefill/decode latency while keeping NCCL utilization high and avoiding harmful microbursts.

Proposal summary:
Implement a Stride-Aligned Prefetch & Comm-Window Manager (SAPC) in the runtime conductor. SAPC maintains lightweight histograms of recent kernel latencies and token-stride patterns per stage and device. From these it computes per-stage lead times and stride boundaries. During prefill and decode, SAPC: (1) issues KV/prefix prefetches with a configurable lead time per-stage, (2) aligns NCCL collective windows to stride boundaries to coalesce small collectives into larger, bandwidth-efficient transfers, and (3) injects bounded backpressure when cross-stage skew exceeds safe thresholds. The manager also exposes a fallback mode that switches to conservative single-stage rendezvous for problematic topologies.

Design details and heuristics:
- Latency model: exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) + variance to predict kernel completion for next stride.
- Stride boundary detection: group token counts into stride bins (configurable) and prefer aligning comms to bin edges to allow deterministic coalescing.
- Comm window sizing: adaptive based on recent NCCL bandwidth utilization and per-GPU queue depths; target at least 2x minimum collective size before issuing.
- Backpressure policy: hierarchical limits (soft/hard). Soft limit triggers lightweight token pacing; hard limit triggers local prefetch throttling + route fallback.
- Kernel selection hints: when SAPC detects consistent overrun on a stage, it emits a kernel selection suggestion (e.g., alternate GEMM kernel variant or quantized path) for the kernel-autotuner to evaluate.

Metrics and targets:
- Primary: reduce warm prefill end-to-end P95 latency by 20% on multi-GPU 4-stage pipelines with mixed batch sizes.
- Secondary: lower GPU stall time by 15% and reduce NCCL small-message count by 40% (increase aggregated payloads).
- Safety: ensure no >5% regression in median decode latency for single-GPU workloads.

Milestones:
1) Design doc + microbench plan (done)
2) Instrumentation & histograms in runtime (ETA 1 sprint)
3) Prototype comm-window algorithm + sim harness (ETA 2 sprints)
4) End-to-end integration and internal canary on dedicated cluster (ETA 3 sprints)
5) Gradual rollout with feature flag + observability dashboards (runtime-1.22)

Trade-offs and risks:
- Coalescing introduces small added latency for the earliest token in a window; mitigated by adaptive lead times and soft limits.
- Heuristics tuning across heterogeneous clusters is nontrivial; we will collect telemetry and auto-calibrate defaults.
- Complex interactions with existing autoscalers and batchers; plan to add non-invasive feature flags and explicit fallback paths.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for stride detection and EWMA-based predictor.
- Microbench: synthetic interconnect with controllable bandwidth/latency to validate coalescing thresholds.
- Canary: run on dedicated canary cluster with production workloads and compare latency/cost matrices.
- Chaos test: inject interconnect jitter and GPU preemption to exercise fallback path.

Observability & rollout:
- New dashboard panels: per-stage predicted lead time, comm-window size distribution, NCCL small-message ratio, per-device stall time.
- Feature flag: runtime.sched.sapc.enabled with rollout by customer/region.

Acceptance criteria:
- SAPC reduces prefill P95 by >=20% on target workload in canary benchmarks.
- No more than 2% increase in token-level cost for hosted API in testbed.
- Code reviewed and merged with at least two engineering approvals and a performance signoff.
